usage: This is the standard, everyday way to introduce yourself in Egyptian Arabic. It is used in both formal and informal situations, regardless of the gender of the speaker or the listener. You simply add your name directly after the word.

variants.label: I am (alternative)
variants.note: A very common and slightly more casual way to introduce yourself instead of saying 'my name is'.

variants.label: What is your name? (to a man)
variants.note: The standard way to ask a male his name after introducing yourself.

variants.label: What is your name? (to a woman)
variants.note: The standard way to ask a female her name.

variants.label: What is your name? (formal, to a man)
variants.note: Used when speaking to someone older or in a professional setting.

responses.english: Welcome / Nice to meet you (to a man).

examples.transliteration: ismi sara, wa enta ismak eih?
examples.english: My name is Sarah, and you, what is your name? (to a man)
Nice to meet you, my name is Mahmoud.
